- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–3% for next period.
- When sentiment is negative (≤0.33) or volatile, model often underestimates; increase forecast by 1–3% to compensate for downward bias.
- After sharp price spikes (e.g., +5%+ in 3–5 days), model frequently overshoots in subsequent days; apply a 2–5 day lag correction, reducing forecast by 2–5% per day.
- If sentiment shifts from positive to negative mid-horizon, model fails to adjust; force a mean-reversion correction toward prior 7-day average.
- For 30-day forecasts, model often overreacts to short-term sentiment swings; cap forecast deviation at ±3% of recent 7-day mean to avoid extreme outliers.
- If sentiment history shows repeated “0.33” or “-0.33” patterns, model underperforms; apply a +1.5% bias correction to forecast for next 3–5 days.
